fragment_A.why: Every sample satisfies the predicate and the verdict is FAIL. `hold` is a claim about a duration; evidence that stops at 4000ms cannot settle a claim about 30000ms. An evaluator implementing hold as all(samples) returns PASS and reproduces the case-002 defect by a different route.

assertions.text: event(billing).published where {{MARKER}} appears anywhere absent through cross_service

fragment_B.why: Same rule. Absence is entirely a claim about the window, so a shortened window is a proportionally weaker claim — and this is the assertion form whose failure mode is permanent green.

fragment_C.why: The baseline. An evaluator cannot pass this case by rejecting every hold.

harness_findings.detail: Two samples across a 30000ms budget at a declared 1000ms interval. The PASS stands under the stated rule; a transient violation between the two samples would pass through untouched.

fragment_D.why: PASS is correct and the finding is mandatory. The evaluator must not invent a density threshold — the interval is DECLARED in the environment binding, which is what makes the shortfall checkable rather than a matter of taste. An evaluator without access to the binding omits this finding and says it did.

conformance_note: Fragments A and C are the pair to test first. They are identical apart from where sampling stopped, and every recorded sample in both is true — so an evaluator that returns the same verdict for them has implemented `hold` as all(samples) and has a second route to the 002 defect.
